_strings.@@79fffd856d81: Family Income Tax Credit — Arizona residents whose total income does not exceed the maximum allowed for their filing status and number of dependents. The credit only reduces tax and cannot be refunded.
_strings.@@a270c63eee7c: Property Tax Credit (Form 140PTC) — Must be an Arizona resident for the entire year and have paid Arizona property tax or rent on a main home during 2023. Must be either (a) age 65 or older by Dec 31, 2023, or (b) under 65 but receiving Title 16 Supplemental Security Income (SSI) payments. Total household income must be under the limits below.
_strings.@@a2cc0666938f: Credit for Increased Excise Taxes — Taxpayer must have an SSN valid for employment, meet the income threshold for their filing status, not be claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer, and not have been sentenced to at least 60 days in a county/state/federal prison during 2023. Married joint filers may claim for a spouse with a valid SSN or ITIN.
_strings.@@a579cb30449c: Treaty conformity — AZ conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from AZ income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the AZ return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Arizona's resident return (Form 140) starts from federal adjusted gross income: line 12 of the 2023 Form 140 is "Federal adjusted gross income," and the AZ DOR instructions state "Arizona gross income is your federal adjusted gross income." Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to the AZ return excluded. AZ then applies only specific statutory additions (Form 140 lines 14-18, including the "Other Additions to Arizona Gross Income" schedule on page 5, which lists items such as the ordinary-income portion of lump-sum distributions excluded federally, items previously deducted for Arizona purposes, and claim-of-right adjustments). No line on Form 140 or its additions schedule adds back federal tax-treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA). Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by Arizona -> conforms. (Caveat: the full page-5 additions schedule was read via .gov search snippets, not the full PDF page, because the form PDFs returned HTTP 403 — see unverified.)
_strings.@@c1c78882979c: Nonresident: Arizona Form 140NR - Nonresident Personal Income Tax Return. Part-year resident: Arizona Form 140PY - Part-Year Resident Personal Income Tax Return.
_strings.@@c2a91cb05cc4: Dependent Tax Credit — Available to taxpayers who claim qualifying dependents (a dependent for federal income tax purposes) on the Arizona return. Credit amount is higher for dependents under age 17. Cannot also claim the same individual as a qualifying parent/grandparent exemption (line 41) or Other Exemption (line 40).
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 140 Line 46: "Tax: Multiply line 45 by 2.5% (.025)" (Line 45 = Arizona taxable income = Line 42 Arizona AGI minus Lines 43-44; Line 12 starts from federal AGI). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($2,100 — Form 140 Line 38: $2,100 per age-65-or-over box (subtracted before Arizona taxable income — Line 42 = line 37 minus lines 38-41). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Line 38.); blind ($1,500 — Form 140 Line 39: $1,500 per blind box. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Line 39.); other ($2,300 — Form 140 Line 40: $2,300 per "Other Exemptions" person. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Line 40.); qualifying_parent_grandparent ($10,000 — Form 140 Line 41: $10,000 per qualifying parent or grandparent — mutually exclusive with the Line 40 other exemption / Line 49 dependent credit for the SAME individual. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Line 41.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Arizona has NO personal exemption, and the plain dependent exemption was replaced by the Line 49 Dependent Tax Credit ($100 per dependent under 17, $25 per dependent 17 or over, phased down 5% per $1,000 when federal AGI exceeds $200,000 — $400,000 MFJ). It is a CREDIT against tax, not a base reduction, and is NOT modeled by calc.state_tax. The 2023 Arizona standard deduction equals the printed 2023 federal amounts. Increased Standard Deduction for charitable contributions (Line 44): non-itemizers may add 31% of qualified charitable contributions (2023 rate, increased from 27%) — NOT modeled; claim it on Line 44. Exemptions on Form 140 lines 38-41 (age 65+ $2,100; blind $1,500; other $2,300; qualifying parent/grandparent $10,000) reduce Arizona AGI on the form — calc.state_tax does not apply them; a 65+/blind filer computes lines 38-41 on the form. Nonresidents (Form 140NR) take the same figures but PRORATED by the line-27 Arizona income ratio (Arizona gross income, line 26, divided by federal AGI, line 25, rounded to three decimal places, not over 1.000): the age-65 ($2,100, line 47), blind ($1,500, line 48) and other ($2,300, line 49) exemptions are totalled on line 50 and multiplied by the ratio on line 51 ("Line 51 - Prorated Exemptions"); "CAUTION: You must prorate the standard deduction" — the standard deduction is multiplied by the ratio on the Standard Deduction Worksheet before it is entered on line 53 (itemizers prorate on Schedule A(NR)); the 31% charitable increase is prorated on page 3 (line 9C = line 7C x the line-8C ratio) before line 54; and "Nonresidents are required to apportion their Dependent Tax Credit" (line 59) by the same ratio. The 2.5% rate (line 56, "Multiply line 55 by 2.5% (.025)") is not prorated. NOT modeled by calc.state_tax. Source: AZ DOR 2023 Form 140NR Instructions p. 9 (line 27), p. 19 (lines 51 and 53), p. 20 (worksheet, line 54, line 56, line 59) — https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/2023-12/FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2023_140NRi.pdf
